small_guidance:
- The conv_transpose dominates runtime (21.8ms with the fused tail kernel); tuning BLOCK/num_warps of the current fused pool+htanh+mean kernel will not move the needle. If staying in tune mode, try BLOCK=4096 with num_warps=8, num_stages=2, and switch the pool kernel to use channels-last reads so the 2x2 window loads coalesce per row.
- Consider one program per (N, C-tile) with C_BLOCK=4 to amortize the launch overhead (N*C=8192 programs currently); a vectorized load of 2 adjacent W elements per iter would halve issued loads.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose2d` with a custom Triton kernel — with stride=1, padding=1, kernel=3 it is equivalent to a regular conv2d on the input with the flipped weight (no scatter needed). Implement as an im2col-style GEMM: program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), gather the 3x3 window implicitly, accumulate into registers. This is the dominant cost and the only path to a large speedup.
- Fuse the entire tail (maxpool 2x2 + hardtanh + spatial mean + tanh) into the conv epilogue: since the output is reduced to (N,C,1,1), have each conv program compute its output tile, immediately apply maxpool+hardtanh, and atomically accumulate the partial sum into a (N,C) buffer; a tiny second kernel scales by 1/(H_out*W_out) and applies tanh. This eliminates the full 128×64×256×256 intermediate write/read.
- Alternatively, since stride=1/pad=1 makes conv_transpose ≡ conv with weight flipped over (kh,kw) and transposed (IC↔OC), precompute the flipped weight in __init__ and run a standard conv2d Triton kernel — simpler than true scatter-add and still satisfies the safety contract (every op runs at runtime on the input).
